title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的头号新闻是 OpenAI 单方面终止与 Cursor 的合作，理由是「信任」。这条消息像一块磁铁，瞬间吸出了整个 coding agent 生态的反应——Replit 抢着收编流失用户，Anthropic 却表态会留下继续合作。而在工具战争的喧嚣之下，今天真正的底层信号有两个：一是数据正在取代模型成为新护城河（Google 花 1000 万美元买下破产航司的数据来训模型）；二是 AI 圈所有「坚定信念」的半衰期都短得惊人，从 Meta 的 Madhu Guru 到 Box 的 Levie，大家都在提醒你——别把任何一套打法当真。

archive.title: Agent 分发之争日报
archive.desc: OpenAI 以「信任」为由终止与 Cursor 合作，coding agent 生态瞬间洗牌；而在这场分发渠道之争背后，数据正在取代模型成为真正的护城河。

sections.title: The Cursor-OpenAI Split / Cursor 与 OpenAI 分手
sections.desc: OpenAI 以「信任」为由终止与 Cursor 的合作，coding agent 市场在一夜之间重新洗牌。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux (Codex & ChatGPT) drops the day's biggest news: OpenAI is ending its partnership with Cursor and will stop providing model access through it, effective November 12, citing 'trust' as the deciding factor.

The announcement is careful to give developers a runway and alternatives: you can keep using your own OpenAI API key, or OpenAI's own IDE extensions for Cursor. OpenAI frames it as doubling down on 'broad optionality' and its own open-source work.
The subtext is the real story: as coding agents become the primary distribution channel for frontier models, control over that channel is becoming a strategic battleground.
original: We unfortunately have decided that we cannot continue providing access to our models through Cursor and are ending our partnership. It boils down to trust and we've asked that this takes effect on November 12 to give you some time to plan.
Many have used the GPT models through Cursor and here are options we know should work in the future: We will continue to allow using your own OpenAI API key...

rewrite: OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux（Codex 和 ChatGPT 团队）抛出了今天最大的新闻：OpenAI 决定终止与 Cursor 的合作，不再通过 Cursor 提供模型访问，将于 11 月 12 日生效，理由是「信任」。
声明给开发者留了缓冲和备选：你可以继续用自己的 OpenAI API key，或者用 OpenAI 官方的 Cursor IDE 扩展。OpenAI 把这次切割包装成对「广泛可选择性」和自身开源计划的加码。
真正的信号在潜台词里：当 coding agent 成为前沿模型的主要分发渠道，对这条渠道的控制权正在变成战略争夺的焦点。
original: 我们不得不做出决定：无法继续通过 Cursor 提供模型访问，终止合作。核心是信任问题，11 月 12 日生效，给你们留时间规划。
很多人在 Cursor 里用过 GPT 模型，以下是可行的替代方案：继续使用你自己的 OpenAI API key……

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad wastes no time turning OpenAI's Cursor exit into an acquisition pitch: OpenAI models are now free on Replit, and Replit's router makes high-end models 'incredibly cost-efficient.'
The sharper line: if you're a business looking for an 'independent, multi-model alternative to Cursor,' Replit will happily fund your transition. This is a land grab, plain and simple.
The competitive reality: the moment one frontier lab pulls out of a third-party agent, every other platform treats it as an opening to convert disaffected developers.
original: You can access OpenAI models on Replit for free. Our router also makes high-end models incredibly cost-efficient.
If you're a business looking for an independent, multi-model alternative to Cursor, we'd be happy to fund your transition.

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 毫不迟疑地把 OpenAI 退出 Cursor 变成了一次获客攻势：OpenAI 模型在 Replit 上现在免费，而且 Replit 的 router 让高端模型「成本效率极高」。
更锋利的一句：如果你是一家正在寻找「独立、多模型替代 Cursor 方案」的公司，Replit 很乐意资助你的迁移。这就是赤裸裸的抢地盘。
竞争现实很清楚：一家前沿实验室一旦从第三方 agent 撤出，其他平台立刻把这当成转化失望开发者的窗口。
original: OpenAI 模型在 Replit 上免费可用。我们的 router 让高端模型成本效率极高。
如果你在找独立、多模型的 Cursor 替代品，我们很乐意资助你迁移。

rewrite: Anthropic's Thariq (Claude Code) responds from the other side of the split with a strikingly different tone: a 'long-time admirer of the Cursor team' who is 'excited to continue to partner with them.'
Where OpenAI pulled out over trust, Anthropic signals it's staying put. The contrast is the story: two frontier labs, opposite strategies for the same distribution channel.
It also quietly reinforces Claude's position inside Cursor — the tool many developers will now lean on even harder.
original: Long-time admirer of the Cursor team, few have done more to bring AI coding to the world. Excited to continue to partner with them.

rewrite: Anthropic 的 Thariq（Claude Code 团队）从这场分手的另一边发声，语气截然不同：他是 Cursor 团队「长期的仰慕者」，并且「很期待继续与他们合作」。
OpenAI 因为信任问题退出，Anthropic 却在表态会留下。这种对比本身就是故事：两家前沿实验室，对同一条分发渠道采取了完全相反的策略。
这也悄然强化了 Claude 在 Cursor 里的位置——很多开发者现在会更依赖它。
original: 我一直仰慕 Cursor 团队，很少有人比他们为 AI coding 的普及做得更多。期待继续与他们合作。

sections.title: Data Is the New Moat / 数据成为新护城河
sections.desc: Google 花 1000 万美元买下破产航司的数据，Eon 联合创始人解释为什么在 AI 时代数据才是真正的护城河。

rewrite: Eon co-founders Ofir Ehrlich and Gonen Stein (ex-AWS, who built CloudEndure and sold it to Amazon) make a sharp case: in the AI era, data — not models or compute — is the only real moat, because models and compute have 'almost zero switching costs.'

The headline example: Google bought Spirit Airlines' data out of bankruptcy for $10 million — not the planes, the data — to train models, with Mercor reportedly the other bidder. They predict we'll see far more of these 'out of bankruptcy data buys.'

On security, they describe a new threat 'on steroids': AI agents with legitimate permissions inside your environment can drop a table in seconds. The methodology is similar to defending against ransomware, but 'the velocity of that happening is extreme.'
Their thesis: everyone can now be a builder, which is both a gift and a governance nightmare — a flood of non-human actors handling sensitive data outside the organization's rules.
original: If you're a company... the most valuable thing that you have is actually your data.

Two days ago you saw Google buy something from the bankrupt Spirit Airlines. They didn't buy airplanes. They bought the data. They bought the data for $10,000,000 because they think it's very important... They're using it to train models.

What we're seeing now on steroids is that the same type of threat is coming from non human actors, from AI agents that essentially have legitimate access to the environment with legitimate permissions... a table is all of a sudden dropped.

rewrite: Eon 的联合创始人 Ofir Ehrlich 和 Gonen Stein（前 AWS，创立了 CloudEndure 并卖给了亚马逊）给出了一个尖锐判断：在 AI 时代，真正的护城河是数据，而不是模型或算力——因为模型和算力「几乎没有切换成本」。
最有冲击力的例子：Google 花了 1000 万美元从破产的 Spirit Airlines 手里买下了数据——不是飞机，是数据——用来训练模型，据说另一个竞标方是 Mercor。他们预测这类「破产数据收购」会越来越多。
安全方面，他们描述了一种「加倍的」新威胁：拥有合法权限的 AI agent 在你的环境里几秒钟就能删掉一张表。方法上和防御勒索软件类似，但「速度是极端的」。
他们的核心论点：现在人人都能当 builder，这既是礼物也是治理噩梦——大量不受组织规则约束的非人类行动者在处理敏感数据。
original: 如果你是一家公司……你拥有的最有价值的东西其实是你的数据。
两天前 Google 从破产的 Spirit Airlines 买了点东西。他们没买飞机，买的是数据。花 1000 万美元是因为他们觉得数据很重要……用来训练模型。
我们现在看到的是加倍的同类威胁，来自非人类行动者、来自拥有合法权限的 AI agent……一张表突然就被删了。

sections.title: The Half-Life of Beliefs / 信念的半衰期
sections.desc: 从 Meta 到 Box，AI 圈领袖都在提醒：任何一套打法、任何一个「坚定信念」的保质期都短得惊人。

rewrite: Madhu Guru, a Senior Director of AI at Meta (previously led Gemini and Veo at Google), argues that AI product building has a '~3-month playbook half-life' — traditional teams discover a playbook and milk it for five years, but AI labs throw playbooks away every few months as returns diminish.
His prescription for builders: define meta-principles for (1) continuously learning what the market wants now versus in three months, and (2) executing with extreme urgency.
The bluntest line: 'Legacy teams are optimized for playbook milking. AI teams need to be optimized for inventing.'
original: AI product building has a ~3-month playbook half-life... Most trad product teams are built to discover a playbook and then milk it for the next 5 years. However in the AI labs, we consciously throw away playbooks every few months cos we start seeing diminishing returns.
Legacy teams are optimized for playbook milking. AI teams need to be optimized for inventing.

rewrite: Meta 的 AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru（之前在 Google 负责 Gemini 和 Veo）认为，AI 产品建设有「约 3 个月的 playbook 半衰期」——传统团队发现一套打法然后吃五年，但 AI 实验室每隔几个月就主动扔掉打法，因为收益开始递减。
他给 builder 开的方子：围绕两条元原则做事——(1) 持续学习市场今天要什么、三个月后可能要什么；(2) 以极致的紧迫感执行。
最扎心的一句：「传统团队为『吃老本』而优化，AI 团队必须为『发明』而优化。」
original: AI 产品建设有约 3 个月的 playbook 半衰期。传统团队发现打法后吃五年，AI 实验室每隔几个月就主动扔打法，因为收益递减。
传统团队为吃老本优化，AI 团队为发明优化。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie makes the same point from the strategy side: the average strongly held belief in AI has a half-life of six months 'at best.' He rattles off beliefs the industry has cycled through without consensus — from 'OSS is too far behind' to 'RAG is dead' to 'AI will decimate engineering jobs.'
The point isn't that these takes are wrong — it's that they're all provisional, and anyone who locks into one conviction will be left behind.
His advice: 'remain flexible in your thinking because we're going to be in a constant state of change for a while.'
original: The average strongly held belief these days in AI has a half life of 6 months at best... The key here is to remain flexible in your thinking because we're going to be in a constant state of change for a while.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 从战略角度说了同一件事：AI 领域平均的「坚定信念」半衰期最多只有 6 个月。他列举了一串行业反复横跳、至今没有共识的观点——从「开源落后太多追不上」到「RAG 已死」到「AI 会摧毁工程师岗位」。
重点不是这些判断都错了，而是它们全都是临时的——任何死守某一个定论的人都会被甩下。
他的建议：「保持思维灵活，因为我们会在一段时间内持续处于变化之中。」
original: 如今 AI 领域平均的坚定信念，半衰期最多 6 个月。关键是保持思维灵活，因为我们会持续处于变化之中。

sections.title: The Agentic Web / 面向 Agent 的 Web
sections.desc: Vercel CEO 画出 web 的两个极端，Peter Yang 则点出非技术人群的 AI 产品终态。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch sketches a two-speed future for the web: one extreme is 'ultra-fancy human experiences' for delight and brand (three.js, typegpu), and the other is 'agent-centric content, data and APIs' — pure, lossless signal for machines, with markdown and MCP as the tip of the iceberg.
His bold prediction: the 'in between' gets subsumed by agents producing just-in-time UI. When you need utilitarian content, it'll be generated for you on demand — 'the agent as the new browser.'
He backs it with data: MCP is 'growing explosively,' and it's not just Vercel's implementation — the mcp-handler npm package shows the broader surge.
original: I see the web evolving in two extremes: 1) ultra-fancy human experiences, in the service of delight, exploration, brand, entertainment... 2) agent-centric content, data and APIs. the opposite end of the spectrum: pure, lossless signal for machines.
The 'in between' is likely to be subsumed by agents producing just-in-time UI... Think of the agent as the new browser in this model.
MCP is growing explosively.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 描绘了 web 的双速未来：一个极端是「极致精美的人类体验」，服务于愉悦、探索、品牌和娱乐（three.js、typegpu 在推动）；另一个极端是「面向 agent 的内容、数据和 API」——给机器用的纯粹、无损信号，markdown 和 MCP 只是冰山一角。
他的大胆预测：中间地带会被「按需生成 UI 的 agent」吞掉。当你需要实用内容时，它会实时为你生成——「agent 就是新浏览器」。
他用数据支撑：MCP 正在「爆炸式增长」，而且不只是 Vercel 一家——mcp-handler npm 包的下载量就是更广范围激增的证明。
original: web 在向两个极端演进：1) 极致精美的人类体验，服务于愉悦、探索、品牌、娱乐……2) 面向 agent 的内容、数据和 API，给机器的纯粹无损信号。
中间地带会被按需生成 UI 的 agent 吞掉。agent 就是这个模型里的新浏览器。
MCP 正在爆炸式增长。

rewrite: Peter Yang's hot take: Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work are 'partial solutions,' while Grok Bot is 'the right end state' for a capable AI agent product for non-technical people.

His reasoning is about mental model: people can easily 'grok' that Grok Bot is a computer running in the cloud, whereas most people can't explain the difference between ChatGPT Work and Codex, or how Claude Cowork actually works.
It's a product-design argument disguised as a tool comparison: adoption hinges on whether a non-technical user can form a correct intuition about what the agent is doing.
original: My hot take is that Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work are partial solutions and that Grok Bot is the right end state for a capable AI agent product for non-technical people. Grok Bot I think people can easily 'grok' that it's a computer that runs in the cloud.

rewrite: Peter Yang 的热点判断：Claude Cowork 和 ChatGPT Work 都只是「部分解」，而 Grok Bot 才是面向非技术人群的 AI agent 产品的「正确终态」。
他的理由在于心智模型：普通人能很容易「grok」（秒懂）Grok Bot 就是一台跑在云端的电脑，但大多数人解释不清 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 的区别，也不懂 Claude Cowork 到底怎么运作。
这其实是一个伪装成工具对比的产品设计论证：采纳与否，取决于非技术用户能否对「agent 到底在干嘛」形成正确的直觉。
original: 我的热点判断：Claude Cowork 和 ChatGPT Work 是部分解，Grok Bot 才是面向非技术人群的正确终态。人们能轻松秒懂 Grok Bot 是一台云端电脑。

sections.title: Judgment & Authenticity / 判断力与真实性
sections.desc: 当 AI 产出泛滥，区分信号与噪声的关键从技术转向人的判断与真实经验。

rewrite: Zara Zhang pushes back on the lazy 'AI-generated = slop' framing: whether something is slop has less to do with whether it's AI-generated and more to do with whether it's informed by specific, unique human experiences and perspectives.
Her kicker: 'There's plenty of human-generated slop.' The corollary is that AI plus genuine human insight is not slop at all — the human input is the filter.
It's a timely counterweight as everyone debates how to keep AI output from drowning out real signal.
original: Whether something is slop or not has less to do with whether it's AI-generated and more to do with whether it is informed by specific, unique human experiences/perspectives. There's plenty of human-generated slop.

rewrite: Zara Zhang 反驳了「AI 生成 = slop（垃圾内容）」这种偷懒的说法：一件事是不是 slop，跟它是否由 AI 生成关系不大，而更取决于它是否注入了具体、独特的人类经验和视角。
她的点睛之笔：「人类自己产出的 slop 也一大堆。」言下之意是，AI 加上真实的人类洞察根本不是 slop——人的输入才是那道过滤器。
在所有人都在争论怎么让 AI 产出别淹没真实信号的当下，这是一记及时的反向提醒。
original: 一件事是不是 slop，跟是否 AI 生成关系不大，更取决于是否注入了具体、独特的人类经验和视角。人类自己产出的 slop 也一大堆。

rewrite: FPV Ventures partner Nikunj Kothari gives founders two blunt pieces of advice: the best pitches don't even need to use the word 'AI,' and AI cannot be the only 'why now' in your pitch.
He's self-aware enough to flag that this is subjective and varies by VC — but 'trust me, it'll help if you get ahead of these two.'
The underlying point: if your company's story is just 'AI exists now,' you don't have a defensible reason to exist. AI is the context, not the thesis.
original: 1) The best pitches don't even need to use the word 'AI'. 2) AI cannot be the only 'why now' for your pitch... it'll help if you get ahead of these two!

rewrite: FPV Ventures 合伙人 Nikunj Kothari 给创始人两条直白的建议：最好的 pitch 甚至不需要用到「AI」这个词；而且 AI 不能是你 pitch 里唯一的「why now」。
他很有自知之明地标注这很主观、因 VC 而异——但「相信我，提前想清楚这两点对你绝对有帮助」。
潜台词是：如果你公司的故事只是「现在有 AI 了」，那你没有一个站得住的理由存在。AI 是背景，不是论点。
original: 1) 最好的 pitch 甚至不需要用 'AI' 这个词。2) AI 不能是你 pitch 里唯一的 'why now'。提前想清楚这两点对你有帮助！
